claims.text: Standard laser powder-bed fusion of high-entropy alloys produces heterogeneous microstructures due to rapid solidification.
Standard laser powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components exhibit residual porosity.
Standard laser powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components exhibit dimensional irregularities.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after each deposited layer will improve dimensional precision.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after each deposited layer will improve mechanical integrity.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after each deposited layer will reduce fabrication-induced defects.
In-situ re-melting produces a more uniform, equiaxed grain structure.
In-situ re-melting reduces porosity and residual stress.
A more uniform grain structure, reduced porosity, and lower residual stress improve layer consolidation and surface regularity.
The secondary laser pass re-liquefies the superficial layer and permits more controlled solidification.
More controlled solidification minimizes microstructural heterogeneity, porosity, and lack-of-fusion defects.
The re-melting pass reduces thermal gradients that contribute to dimensional inaccuracies.
The re-melting mechanism produces denser and mechanically more robust layers.
Relative to standard additive manufacturing without re-melting, the intervention will reduce dimensional deviations by approximately 15–25%.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will increase yield strength and ductility.
The benefits apply to parts up to 5 mm thick when laser power and scan speed are optimized in an inert atmosphere.
Extreme geometries or substantially thicker sections may receive less benefit because uniform re-melting energy distribution may not be maintained.
